title: Accelerated quantum Monte Carlo simulations of the attractive Hubbard model on the kagome lattice
authors: Jie Zhang, Xiang Li, Yu Wang
abstract: The recent discovery of several families of kagome materials and experimental realization of optical kagome lattices have stimulated growing numerical studies of interaction-driven correlated states on the kagome lattice. Among the available numerical approaches, determinant quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) is a powerful method for investigating such strongly correlated states. However, the accessible system sizes of existing DQMC simulations remain limited, preventing reliable finite-size scaling analyses. Here we develop a general acceleration scheme based on fast Fourier transform (FFT) for propagator multiplications on composite lattices and combine it with the delay-update algorithm, enabling simulations on system sizes twice as large as those of previous DQMC studies, allowing reliable finite-size scaling analyses of the attractive kagome-lattice Hubbard model. Our large-scale simulations reveal the interaction-driven zero-temperature superfluid quantum criticality at the Dirac filling and provide reliable estimates of the associated critical exponents. Besides, we find no evidence that the previously proposed triangle-rule charge-density-wave order survives in the thermodynamic limit, suggesting that it is likely a finite-size effect. Moreover, for system sizes accessible in current two-dimensional optical lattice experiments, the combined FFT and delay-update scheme exhibits an effective computational cost scaling as $N^{2.49}$, substantially below the $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$ computational cost of conventional DQMC simulations.
summary: This work significantly advances the study of correlated electrons on the kagome lattice by developing an FFT-accelerated Quantum Monte Carlo method. The research confirms superfluid quantum criticality at specific fillings while demonstrating that proposed CDW orders are likely artifacts of finite system size. This computational breakthrough allows for precise determination of critical exponents.
main_problem: The study investigates interaction-driven correlated states, specifically the competition between superfluid (SF) and charge-density-wave (CDW) orders on the kagome lattice.
main_result: Large-scale simulations reveal zero-temperature superfluid quantum criticality at the Dirac filling, while evidence suggests that previously proposed CDW orders are likely finite-size effects.
method: The authors developed and applied an accelerated Determinant Quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) scheme combining FFT techniques with delay-update algorithms to overcome previous computational limitations.
model_or_system: The system is the attractive Hubbard model defined on the kagome lattice, characterized by a Hamiltonian involving nearest-neighbor hopping ($t$) and an attractive interaction ($U < 0$).
key_observables: Superfluid order parameter (P), correlation ratio ($R_{	ext{Pair}}$), and momentum-dependent CDW order parameter ($D(\vec{Q})$).
important_parameters: Dirac filling ($ho = 2/3$), critical interaction $|U|_c \approx 4.79$, and system sizes up to $L=24$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the accelerated DQMC scheme accurately models the physics, allowing for reliable finite-size scaling analyses.
figures_summary: Figures compare computational time scaling (FFT vs. DGEMM) and show data collapse for SF order parameters at $ho=2/3$. Other figures illustrate finite-size extrapolations of CDW order parameters at wave vectors $\Gamma$ and K.
paper_structure: The paper details the model setup, introduces the FFT-accelerated DQMC methodology (combining FFT with delay updates), presents results on SF criticality via finite-size scaling, and concludes by analyzing the stability of various CDW states.
why_interesting: The development of an $N^{2.49}$ computational scaling for a complex QMC simulation is highly relevant, providing access to larger systems than previously possible for studying quantum critical points in lattice models.
